text: Maelduin is an Irish hero, the subject of a famous voyage poem. His name is also written Maeldun, Maeldúin, Maol Dúin, Mael Dúin, or Maeldune. The poem is one of the most famous voyage tales of ancient Ireland. Scribes recorded it variously in the ninth and the eleventh centuries. Maelduin was born of violence. His father raped a nun, who then died giving birth to him. His aunt raised him and told him the story of his conception and birth. In an epic sometimes called the Irish Odyssey, Maelduin set off for the land of the Vikings. He went to avenge his father, killed by those invaders. Sixty warriors attended the young man. They met giant ants, monster cats, and other extraordinary beings. They came to an Otherworld island, where they all found fairy lovers. Such mistresses were notoriously hard to leave. Maelduin's group nearly remained their captives for eternity. In the end they returned to the human world.
